Expiry: a hit requires entry is not None and now < entry['expires_at'] (cache.py:8), with expires_at = now + TTL, TTL=30 (cache.py:2,11). The boundary is strict: at now == expires_at the entry is stale and re-read from db. discard_expired uses <= (cleanup.py:3), so it deletes exactly at the boundary — consistent, but cleanup is not called by fetch_profile.

Update: replace_profile writes to db, then increments versions[identity] (writes.py:2-4). The old cache entry is never deleted; it is orphaned because the next read computes a new key with generation+1 and misses, re-reading db (cache.py:6-11).

DB failure: db.write is line 2, before the version bump, so an exception propagates and the generation is not incremented — the old key stays valid and reads keep returning the pre-update value until TTL expiry. No rollback/compensation exists.

Freshness: not guaranteed. The read path is check-then-act with no locking (cache.py:7-11), so concurrent readers can both miss and both write; a reader that fetched generation N before a concurrent update can repopulate the stale key after the bump, though that key is then unreachable.
